findings.title: A RoleBinding cannot grant a cluster-wide request
findings.cause: container dashboard exits because the API server refuses its ServiceAccount app: it may not list pods across the cluster. RoleBinding app-reads-pods grants it, through Role pod-reader, in namespace kd-rbac-all-namespaces only, and the request is across all namespaces (or of a resource that belongs to no namespace), which only a ClusterRoleBinding grants; its log says: "Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:kd-rbac-all-namespaces:app\" cannot list resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" at the cluster scope"; Deployment pod-dashboard has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container dashboard exited with code 1 (Error), restarted 6 times
last lines of container dashboard's log (current run)
evidence.detail: Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:kd-rbac-all-namespaces:app" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" at the cluster scope

evidence.what: Role pod-reader, bound by RoleBinding app-reads-pods: apiGroups [""], resources ["pods"], verbs ["get", "list", "watch"]
evidence.command: kubectl get role pod-reader -n kd-rbac-all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{.rules}'

evidence.what: RoleBinding app-reads-pods grants Role pod-reader to ServiceAccount app

findings.fix: If the app needs only namespace kd-rbac-all-namespaces, have it read that namespace (kubectl -n kd-rbac-all-namespaces instead of -A, or an informer for one namespace); if it needs every namespace, create a ClusterRole with the rule and bind it with a ClusterRoleBinding to ServiceAccount kd-rbac-all-namespaces/app.
